_comment: Guided tour of the FRET line generator. Steps point at real controls (a spec field's attr, a button's action, a table); the ones that need the user's hands wait for them.

steps.title: What a FRET line tells you
steps.text:
A static species sits on its static line in the E-τ_F plot. A molecule exchanging between two states within the burst bows towards longer lifetimes, onto a dynamic line. We draw one of each.

The tool starts with one FD (Gaussian) component, which is what the static line needs.

steps.title: Step 1: choose what varies
steps.text:
In the Sweep tab, Vary is set to the mean distance C0 ... RDA0. Set Min to 20 and Max to 120 Å, and τ_D0 to your donor-only lifetime (4 ns if you have none).

The Gaussian width s0 in the editor is the linker width, which bends the line away from the diagonal. 6 Å is typical.

steps.title: Step 2: compute the static line
steps.text: Press Add FRET line. The orange curve is the static line. At τ_F = 2 ns it sits near E = 0.56, while the diagonal 1 - τ_F/τ_D0 gives 0.50.

steps.title: Step 3: a second state
steps.text: On the Components tab press Add for a second FD (Gaussian). In the editor, set component C0's RDA0 to one state (for example 40 Å) and C1's to the other (70 Å): select a row to edit that component.

steps.title: Step 4: sweep the fraction
steps.text: Back on Sweep, set Vary to fraction · C0, Min 0 and Max 1, then press Add FRET line again. The new curve joins the static line at both states and bows out between them: a population in that gap exchanges within the burst.

steps.title: Use the lines
steps.text: Save CSV writes every line (τ_F, τ_X, E per point). The FRET lines tab lists them: untick Show to hide one, Remove to delete it. Push to ndX overlays them on every open ndX window.
